key_insight: Detonation-sprayed Ni–Cr–Fe–B–Si–C self-fluxing coatings are highly sensitive to gas ratio, barrel fill, and shot timing, with lower fill improving density while higher O/C and longer delays improve wear resistance and surface finish.
engineering_relevance: The results provide a parameter window for restoring and hardening machine parts by balancing friction reduction, hardness, porosity, and wear life in detonation-sprayed coatings.
method: Adjusted working-gas molar ratio O/C from 1.026 to 1.856
Changed inter-shot delay from 0 to 1 s during detonation spraying
evidence_signal: The abstract reports lamellar coating microstructures, friction and wear testing, roughness measurements, and hardness values up to 905.6 HV, with specific wear rate reduced to 0.000189 mm³/(N·m).
watch_item: Conditions that minimize friction can also increase wear and residual-stress cracking, so process optimization must trade off tribology against coating integrity.
paper_title: Development of a Method for Producing Self-Fluxing Nickel-Based Coatings by Detonation Spraying
